deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the thermodynamic preliminaries (§1) of Riemann's 1860 memoir 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. The right-hand scratch work belongs to the integration method of that memoir (the Riemann-function method for the linear equation satisfied by w).

(A) Pressure–density law. Riemann notes that the Mariotte (Boyle) law p ∝ ρ was previously assumed. That assumption is justified only if the temperature changes produced by compression equalise so fast that the temperature can be treated as constant. A struck sentence says heat exchange between neighbouring layers is probably negligible. Therefore one must use the law for a gas that neither absorbs nor gives off heat, i.e. the adiabatic law.

(B) Equation of state. Let v be the volume of unit weight, p the pressure and T the absolute temperature counted from −273°. Mariotte plus Gay-Lussac give pv = RT, i.e. log p + log v = log T + const.

(C) Heat absorbed. Regard T as a function T(p,v). Let c be the specific heat at constant pressure and c' at constant volume, both per unit weight. When p and v change by dp and dv, the heat absorbed is
 dQ = c (∂T/∂v)_p dv + c' (∂T/∂p)_v dp.
Since ∂log T/∂log v = ∂log T/∂log p = 1, this gives
 dQ = T (c dlog v + c' dlog p).

(D) Adiabatic law. Setting dQ = 0 gives dlog p = −(c/c') dlog v. With Poisson's assumption that k = c/c' is independent of T and p, this integrates to
 log p = −k log v + const, i.e. p v^k = const.
Riemann adds that the experiments of Regnault, Joule and Thomson make these laws very nearly valid for O2, N2, H2 and their mixtures over all attainable pressures and temperatures. The sentence 'Nach Regnault ist für diese Gase …' is left unfinished; the previous page has the numbers 1.421, 1.410 and 423.55.

(E) Mayer's hypothesis. Consider an isothermal change (my inference: dlog p = −dlog v). Then dQ = T(c − c') dlog v. Mayer's hypothesis equates the mechanical equivalent of this heat with the external work:
 A T (c − c') dlog v = p dv.
Since p dv = p v dlog v, this gives
 c − c' = p v/(A T),
which is Mayer's relation c_p − c_v = R/A. Here A is the mechanical equivalent of the heat unit.

(F) Right-hand scratch: a characteristic (Goursat) problem.
 w_rs = f(r+s) w, with w = 1 on r = r' and on s = s'.
This is the kind of auxiliary function Riemann constructs (the 'Riemann function') to solve the linear equation for w. The previous page tries the ansatz w = F((p−p')(q−q')ψ(σ)).
- Since w ≡ 1 on s = s', we have w_r(r,s') = 0. Integrating in s gives
 w_r(r,s) = ∫_{s'}^{s} f(r+σ) w(r,σ) dσ.
- He then begins an integration by parts:
 ∫_{s'}^{s} g dσ = (s−s') g(s) − ∫_{s'}^{s} (σ−s') g'(σ) dσ, with g = f(r+σ)w.
- Differentiating under the integral sign gives
 w_rr = ∫_{s'}^{s} [f'(r+σ) w + f(r+σ) w_r] dσ.
- Substituting w_r from above produces a double integral ∫∫ f(r+σ) w dr dσ. This looks like the start of a successive-approximation (Picard-type) or iterated-integral treatment.
The fragment breaks off.
errors: No substantive mathematical errors. The heat expression, the adiabatic law and Mayer's relation are all correct.

The integration-by-parts fragment as transcribed reads '+∫ (s−s')…'. The correct sign of the remainder is minus: (s−s')g(s) − ∫(σ−s')g'(σ)dσ. Either the transcription or Riemann's scratch has the sign or the factor garbled; the fragment is incomplete in any case.
The step dlog p = −(c/c') dlog v ⇒ p v^k = const relies on Poisson's assumption that k is constant. Riemann states this assumption explicitly, so the step is not unjustified.
Mayer's relation is written as derived from an isothermal change. The isothermal condition (dlog p = −dlog v) is used implicitly but not written.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of material Riemann published in 1860. The thermodynamic part is textbook (Poisson, Mayer), and the Riemann-function scratch is his known method. The only mildly interesting detail is the attempt to treat w_rs = f(r+s)w via iterated integrals, a hint toward successive approximation, but it is fragmentary.

transcription_corrections: 'sich [?] schnell ausgleichen' should read 'sich so schnell ausgleichen'.
In the struck sentence, read 'daß der Wärmeaustausch zwischen den angrenzenden Luftschichten …', not 'die Wärmeaustausch'.
'Nach [-...-] Versuchen von Regnault' is probably 'Nach den neueren Versuchen von Regnault, Joule und Thomson'.

The first formula is c (∂T/∂v) dv + c' (∂T/∂p) dp, with c paired with ∂/∂v. The struck right-hand side T(c dlog v + c' dlog p) is rewritten on the next line as the result, preceded by 'oder, da ∂log T/∂log v = ∂log T/∂log p = 1'.

'Hypothese Mayers [?]' corresponds to the struck 'Mayer'sche Hypothese'. The sentence 'daß das mechanische Äquivalent der aufgenommenen Wärmemenge …' is left grammatically unfinished, and the formula A T(c−c') dlog v = p dv completes it.

The right-hand margin fragment reads approximately: ∂w/∂r = ∫_{s'}^{s} f(r+s)w ds = (s−s') f(r+s)w + ∫ … (an integration-by-parts attempt). The next line, ∂²w/∂r² = ∫_{s'}^{s} [f'(r+s)w + f(r+s) ∂w/∂r] ds, continues as ∫∫ f(r+s)w dr ds, written beside it.
